producer_report.summary: I removed the stub gate that made the stub log starts in the expected order, and replaced the test's plain-case check. The test now asserts that `report.plan_groups.concat()` equals u1..u6,s1,s2, which the drain decides deterministically. It also asserts that s1's start index is at least 4. With 3 workers, `take_until_done` pops and logs an item before it pops the next, so s1 cannot start in the first four. The other assertions are unchanged. I rewrote the changelog entry to give the pop-then-log cause, a possible failure log with s1 at index 4, and the three jobs. It states that no failure and no never-finishing run was reproduced in this job. I did not reproduce the original failure by running the test repeatedly under load (the shell policy blocked loops). I also did not run a mutation check. The cause comes from reading the code.
